examples.en: I buy books online.
I bought a new computer last week.
To buy a ticket, please line up over there.
Where did you buy that bag?

examples.ko: 이 제품은 매장에서만 구입할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can buy this product only in stores.
The clothes I bought were small, so I went to exchange them.

explain: '사다'와 뜻이 같지만 더 격식 있는 말이라 안내문, 쇼핑몰, 뉴스에서 자주 보여요. 친구와 말할 때는 '샀어요'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. 짝말은 파는 쪽의 '판매하다'예요.
explain_en: It means the same as '사다' but sounds more formal, so you see it in notices, online shops and the news. With friends, '샀어요' is much more natural. Its counterpart on the seller's side is '판매하다'.

dis.h: buy a thing, general and neutral

p.n: Both are fine; 구매하다 sounds a bit more like online or consumer buying.

examples.en: The delivery food came with wooden chopsticks.
Split the wooden chopsticks in half and use them.
You use wooden chopsticks once and throw them away.
For lunch I ate cup noodles with wooden chopsticks and enjoyed it.
Please give me two more pairs of wooden chopsticks.
A splinter from the wooden chopsticks got stuck in my hand.

explain: 한 번 쓰고 버리는 일회용 젓가락이에요. 보통 붙어 있는 걸 반으로 쪼개서 써요. 세는 말은 '벌'이고, 금속 젓가락은 '쇠젓가락'이라고 해요.
explain_en: These are disposable chopsticks, usually joined together so that you split them apart before use. You count them with 벌, and metal chopsticks are called '쇠젓가락'.

examples.en: I bought a digital camera to take on a trip.

examples.ko: 디지털카메라로 찍으면 바로 확인할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you shoot with a digital camera, you can check right away.
Nowadays people take photos with their phones more than with digital cameras.
The digital camera battery has run out.
This digital camera is small and light.
About a thousand photos fit on the digital camera.

explain: 줄여서 '디카'라고 많이 말해요. 필름을 쓰는 '필름 카메라'와 구별할 때 써요. 외래어라서 보통 붙여 써요.
explain_en: It is often shortened to '디카'. You use it to distinguish it from a film camera. As a loanword, it is normally written without spaces.

examples.en: The weather warmed up, so I took out my spring clothes.
I needed new spring clothes, so I went shopping.
It's still chilly, so I get cold in just spring clothes.

examples.ko: 겨울옷은 넣고 봄옷은 옷장 앞쪽에 걸었어요.
examples.en: I put away winter clothes and hung spring clothes at the front of the closet.

examples.ko: 봄옷 세일을 해서 두 벌 샀어요.
examples.en: There was a spring clothes sale, so I bought two pieces.
I changed into spring clothes and my body feels light.

explain: 계절 이름 뒤에 '옷'을 붙여 여름옷, 가을옷, 겨울옷처럼 말해요. 환절기에는 옷장을 정리하면서 '봄옷을 꺼내다', '겨울옷을 넣다'라고 자주 말해요.
explain_en: Adding '옷' after a season name gives words like 여름옷, 가을옷 and 겨울옷. When the seasons change and you tidy the closet, you often say '봄옷을 꺼내다' or '겨울옷을 넣다'.

examples.ko: 선배는 거래처와 통화하는 노하우를 아낌없이 알려 주었다.
examples.en: My senior generously shared his know-how for phone calls with clients.

examples.ko: 오랜 노하우 덕분에 그 가게의 김치찌개는 맛이 깊어요.
examples.en: Thanks to long-built know-how, that shop's kimchi stew has a deep flavor.

examples.ko: 영업 사원들의 노하우를 모아서 신입 사원용 자료를 만들었다.
examples.en: We gathered the sales staff's know-how and made materials for new employees.

examples.ko: 이 요리법은 할머니만의 노하우라서 쉽게 알려 주지 않으세요.
examples.en: This recipe is my grandmother's own know-how, so she doesn't share it easily.

examples.ko: 그 분야의 노하우는 하루아침에 쌓이지 않아요.
examples.en: Know-how in that field isn't built up overnight.

explain: '노하우'는 경험으로 쌓은 요령과 기술이에요. '노하우를 쌓다/전수하다/공유하다'로 자주 써요. '비법'은 남에게 잘 알려 주지 않는 특별한 방법이라서 조금 달라요.

dict_examples.ko: 그 기업은 다년간 축적된 노하우를 바탕으로 빠르게 사세를 확장해 갔다.
dict_examples.en: Based on know-how accumulated over many years, that company expanded rapidly.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 한국의 재벌들이 벤처 자본을 미국에 투자했다 실패한 이유는, 돈 이외에 필요한 노하우와 자질을 갖추지 못했기 때문이다.
dict_examples.en: The reason Korean conglomerates failed when they invested venture capital in the US is that they lacked the know-how and qualities needed besides money.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 물론 자체 개발 기술인 까닭에 기술 수준은 떨어질지 모르지만 그동안 축적해 놓은 노하우는 상당하다.
dict_examples.en: Of course, since it is in-house technology, the technical level may be lower, but the know-how accumulated in the meantime is considerable.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 노하우 is the knack and skill built through experience. It goes with 노하우를 쌓다 (build), 전수하다 (pass on) and 공유하다 (share). 비법 is a bit different: a special method one doesn't readily tell others.

examples.en: My maternal grandparents' house is a two-story house with a yard.

examples.ko: 언젠가 바다가 보이는 이층집에서 살고 싶어요.
examples.en: Someday I want to live in a two-story house with an ocean view.

examples.ko: 이층집으로 이사한 뒤 계단 오르내리기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: Since moving to a two-story house, going up and down the stairs is tiring.

examples.ko: 옆집이 이층집이라 햇빛이 잘 안 들어요.
examples.en: The house next door is two stories, so not much sunlight comes in.
Children waved from the balcony of the two-story house.
That two-story house has a red roof.

explain: '이층집'은 건물 전체가 2층인 단독주택을 말해요. 아파트의 2층에 사는 경우에는 그냥 '이층'이라고 해요. 숫자로 '2층집'이라고 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: '이층집' means a detached house that is two stories tall. If you live on the second floor of an apartment building, you just say '이층'. It can also be written with a number, '2층집'.

examples.en: We lit the candles on the cake and sang a song.
The wind came in through the window and the candle went out.

examples.ko: 분위기 있게 촛불 아래에서 저녁을 먹었어요.
examples.en: We had dinner under candlelight for the atmosphere.
When the power went out, I lit the room with a candle.

examples.ko: 작은 촛불 하나가 방 안을 따뜻하게 만들어요.
examples.en: One small candle makes the room feel warm.

examples.ko: 향기 나는 촛불은 방 분위기를 바꿔 줘요.
examples.en: A scented candle changes the mood of a room.

explain: '초'는 물건 자체이고 '촛불'은 타고 있는 불꽃이에요. 생일에는 '초를 꽂다', '촛불을 켜다/끄다'처럼 동사가 달라요. 소리 낼 때는 ㅂ이 세게 나서 [초뿔]처럼 읽어요.

phrases.example: 많은 사람이 광장에 모여 촛불을 들었어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 촛불을 들고 모여 뜻을 밝히거나 추모하는 집회에 참가한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means taking part in a gathering where people hold candles to voice an opinion or mourn.

explain_en: '초' is the candle itself and '촛불' is the burning flame. On a birthday you 'stick in' a candle ('초를 꽂다') but 'light' or 'blow out' the flame ('촛불을 켜다/끄다'). When said aloud the ㅂ is tensed, so it sounds like [초뿔].

examples.en: I like tomato pasta the most.
I made pasta at home and ate it for lunch.
The pasta is really good at this restaurant.

examples.ko: 파스타 면은 몇 분 동안 삶아요?
examples.en: How many minutes do you boil the pasta noodles?
How about pasta for dinner tonight?
I sprinkled cheese on the warm pasta and ate it.

explain: '스파게티'는 파스타의 한 종류인데, 한국에서는 식당 메뉴에 '파스타'라고 적는 곳이 많아요. 면은 '삶다', 요리는 '만들다'라고 해요. 소스에 따라 '토마토 파스타', '크림 파스타'처럼 이름을 붙여요.
explain_en: '스파게티' is one kind of pasta, but many Korean restaurant menus simply list '파스타'. The noodles are '삶다' (boil) and the dish is '만들다' (make). Names follow the sauce, as in '토마토 파스타' and '크림 파스타'.

examples.en: Our team splits the parts and presents.
I took the high part in the choir.
This part is sure to be on the exam.

examples.ko: 파트별로 연습한 뒤에 같이 맞춰 봐요.
examples.en: We practice part by part and then try it together.
The last part of the movie was a little boring.
Many students work part-time at cafes.

explain: 책이나 영상의 한 구간은 '부분'이나 '단원'과 비슷하게 쓰고, 합창·밴드에서 맡은 몫은 '파트'가 거의 정해진 말이에요. 회사에서는 팀 아래 작은 단위를 '파트'라고 부르기도 해요. 시간제 일은 '파트타임'이라고 해요.
explain_en: For a section of a book or video it overlaps with '부분' or '단원', but for the role you take in a choir or band, '파트' is the set word. Companies sometimes call a small unit under a team a '파트'. A short-hours job is '파트타임'.
